key_findings: Kayra/Tengri as sky deity confirmed in Orkhon inscriptions (primary source, 8th century)
Umay goddess documented in Orkhon + Altai epics + Mongolian shamanism (linguistic/theological continuity across Altaic peoples)
Dualistic cosmology (Ülgen good/sky vs. Erlik evil/underworld) attested across Altaic traditions
Orkhon inscriptions depict minimalist Tengri worship (distant deity, no elaborate ritual detail)
Modern Tengriism reconstruction incorporates elements ABSENT from Orkhon sources (elaborate rituals, doctrinal hierarchies)
MAJOR HISTORIOGRAPHIC ISSUE: Gap between primary sources (Orkhon, minimalist) and modern reconstruction (elaborate) creates authenticity debate — 'invention of tradition' or legitimate recovery?

historiographic_central_debate.question: Is modern Tengriism a legitimate recovery of pre-Islamic Turkish religion or an 'invention of tradition' serving nationalist agendas?

competing_schools.position: Tengri worship was central to pre-Islamic Turkic religion; Orkhon inscriptions accurately represent core beliefs
competing_schools.modern_status: foundational but superseded by critical analysis

competing_schools.position: Orkhon represents elite ideology, not popular belief; shamanism coexisted with Tengri worship
Modern Tengriism reconstructs fragmented sources into false monolith; serves contemporary nationalist agendas; 'authentic recovery' claim is dubious
Tengriism represents legitimate recovery and continuation of authentic pre-Islamic Turkish tradition

authenticity_debate_summary.core_issue: Source gap between Orkhon (primary, 8th century, minimalist) and modern Tengriism (elaborate ritual, doctrinal hierarchy)
interpretation_problems: Gap could reflect: (a) later written sources omitted oral traditions, (b) rituals developed after Orkhon period, (c) Islamic influence added complexity, (d) modern inventions
No way to adjudicate between these without new primary sources
Methodological debate: how to reconstruct unattested religious systems?
authenticity_debate_summary.scholarly_consensus: Modern Tengriism is contemporary religious movement (21st century) inspired by pre-Islamic traditions but not simple continuation of unbroken transmission
